title: Koerkenmeier v. Illiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained: the SJC answered the issue 'Yes'—Illiana Presbytery erred in appointing a Commission with broad power 'to deal with matters' at CGPC—but held the error harmless because the Commission did not exercise the broad grant and acted only as an investigating and recommending committee, and the CGPC Session endorsed the report's wisdom. Judgment: 'it was harmless error for which no remedy is necessary.' No rescission, invalidation, or other relief ordered. Adopted 20 concurred, 4 absent.
first_summary: The SJC sustained a complaint against Illiana Presbytery for appointing a commission with broad power to 'deal with matters' at Center Grove Presbyterian Church, holding the broad charge could usurp the session's original jurisdiction under BCO 11-3 & 4 and 33-1. It said a limited investigative committee under BCO 13-9(f) and 31-2 would have been proper.
summary: Illiana Presbytery appointed a commission with broad power 'to deal with matters' at Center Grove Presbyterian Church after a pastor requested inquiry into alleged evils. The SJC sustained the complaint but held the error harmless: the broad charge could take original jurisdiction from the session contrary to BCO 11-3 & 4 and 33-1, while a limited investigative committee under BCO 13-9(f) and 31-2 would have been proper. Because the commission never exercised that power and the session endorsed its findings, no remedy, including invalidation of the adopted report, was ordered.

evidence_notes.dispute: Complaint challenged Illiana Presbytery's Sept. 3, 2009 appointment of a commission with broad power to deal with matters at CGPC and its Oct. 17, 2009 adoption of the commission report, alleging violation of Preliminary Principle 6 and BCO 11-4 because the session and congregation had not consented to relinquish jurisdiction (lines 17–77, 85–87, pp. 538–541).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Issue answered 'Yes, but it was harmless error for which no remedy is necessary' (lines 75–81). The SJC reasoned Presbytery erred in giving the commission broad power 'to deal with matters' because it could assume original jurisdiction contrary to BCO 11-3 & 4 and 33-1; a committee limited to investigation under BCO 13-9(f) and 31-2 would have been proper. Error was harmless because complainants conceded the commission did not exercise the broad power, acted only as a committee, and the session agreed with the report's wisdom (lines 95–108, pp. 541–543).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Respondent Presbytery filed no brief, so its arguments are not set out (line 89). The complainants' concession on non-exercise of the broad power was material to harmless error; the session's response agreed with the 'wisdom' without necessarily agreeing with process (lines 101–108). No separate dissent appears; four commissioners were absent (line 118).
